visual.source: Native NSHostingView captures with synthetic local usage matching the observed 35987-token sample
visual.grayscaleMethod: Core Image desaturation of the complete native capture, followed by pixel channel checks; system accessibility preferences were not changed
visual.reviewScope: Visible native viewports and static states, not full scrolling, keyboard focus, live billing or VoiceOver. Full-desktop UI-test screenshots remain local and are not sanitized fixtures.

interactive.harness: GrokUITests with Debug-only GrokUIFixtures and unique defaults suites

latest.interpretation: Six synthetic UI cases pass on the final test build. Preflight and postflight found no other UI runner; this is not continuous desktop-exclusivity monitoring. No live billing, credentials or real Grok home were used.

earlierAttempts.finding: Another runner started after preflight. Not an exclusive-desktop pass despite the artifact filename; product and harness defects were subsequently diagnosed separately.
Corrected test-only AXLabel versus AXValue assertion. Also observed other UI runners and a disabled application accessibility tree; that does not prove a system menu was open.
Focused empty/error rerun could not discover the preview quota node while another UI runner was active. This alone does not prove the visible preview was lost.
Inline preview, concrete AX container, Grok-only button trait, opt-in Escape shortcut and viewport-aware test scrolling verified.
UI subset: new cancellation and stale-retention tests passed. Settings failure queried another NowPlayingQA app; celebration was observed but AX scrolling outlasted its lifetime before click.

Focused Settings and celebration rerun passed, including Done dismissal. Once-only notification is tested separately from persistent badge navigation; transient-banner click is not certified. Production timing unchanged.

interactive.visualSpotCheck: Native matrix reviewed separately. XCTest verifies scoped Settings/preview routes, cancellation, stale/unknown/error states and once-only notification; it does not certify all accessibility flows, the actual Dock hover route or live billing.
